exposure: Intravenous magnesium sulphate at two different dosages (30 mg/kg and 50 mg/kg)
Magnesium sulphate dosage (0 mg/kg control, 30 mg/kg, 50 mg/kg)
outcome: Adverse events (e.g., nausea, vomiting, dyspnea, respiratory depression, chest discomfort, drowsiness, shivering, dysrhythmia, bradycardia, hypotension)
cohort: 90 female patients, classified as ASA grade I and II, aged between 20 and 40 years, scheduled for infraumbilical surgeries (specifically lower segment caesarean section) under spinal anaesthesia.
finding: Intravenous magnesium sulphate at a dosage of 50 mg/kg during spinal anaesthesia significantly prolonged analgesia duration, reduced postoperative pain, and decreased analgesic requirements compared to a lower dose (30 mg/kg) and placebo, without significant adverse effects.
